t:
(a) Contract Authority.—Section 560 of division D of the Consolidated and Further Continuing Appropriations Act, 2013 (Public Law 113–6) is repealed. 
    (b) Partnership Pilot Program.—Section 559 of division F of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2014 (6 U.S.C. 211 note; Public Law 113–76) is repealed.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the heading "Partnership Pilot Program" signals coordination with outside partners. But the section only repeals two earlier appropriations provisions. It creates no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: (b) Partnership Pilot Program.—Section 559 of division F of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2014 (6 U.S.C. 211 note; Public Law 113–76) is repealed.

qwen_block.w: This section merely repeals two previous statutory provisions regarding contract authority and a pilot program. It does not establish any new process for consultation, public comment, or coordination with outside parties. The repeal of a program does not constitute participation in a decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: (a) Contract Authority.—Section 560 of division D of the Consolidated and Further Continuing Appropriations Act, 2013 (Public Law 113–6) is repealed. (b) Partnership Pilot Program.—Section 559 of division F of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2014 (6 U.S.C. 211 note; Public Law 113–76) is repealed.

opus.w: This section only repeals two earlier statutory provisions and sets up no process for outside parties to take part in a federal decision. The word "Partnership" is just part of the repealed program's name. If anything, the repeal removes a channel for outside involvement rather than creating one.
opus.s: (b) Partnership Pilot Program.—Section 559 of division F of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2014 (6 U.S.C. 211 note; Public Law 113–76) is repealed.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** The tempting reading is that "Partnership Pilot Program" means working with private parties or local governments, since the original Section 559 let U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) partner with outside entities. That reading fails because this section only repeals two earlier provisions. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue, and nobody outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision here.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely repeals two previous statutory provisions. It does not create any new requirement for the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or receive input from parties outside the federal government. The repeal of a 'Partnership Pilot Program' does not itself constitute participation.

    (b) Partnership Pilot Program.—Section 559 of division F of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2014 (6 U.S.C. 211 note; Public Law 113–76) is repealed.

Resolution: The section only repeals previous laws; it does not establish any new process for participation, consultation, or coordination with outside parties. Repealing a statute does not itself constitute participation.
